subject: Post-call: capability summary + streaming coherence & eval plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Park <anna.park@clearmedhealth.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: capability summary + streaming coherence & eval plan

Hi Anna — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Call highlights (30 min):
- Product: Your team runs conversational triage for patient intake and billing Q&A; main pain is partial answers being presented to users mid-stream which cause follow-up confusion.
- Metrics priority: user-reported accuracy (subjective), first-helpful-token latency, and stop-sequence correctness for forms.
- Data: sample transcripts (~2k rows) and a small synthetic set you shared.

Redwood recommendations (initial):
1) Model candidates to evaluate: rw-instruct-3b (fast, lower cost), rw-guanaco-13b-q4 (balance of quality/latency), rw-llama-70b-q8 (higher quality, higher cost). We propose starting with the 13b quantized variant for streaming baseline.
2) Streaming UX checks: streaming partial-output coherence (we'll measure incoherent cutoff events), stop-sequence pass-rate for your form templates, and median time-to-first-token for a 64-token reply. Target: median TTF token <= 150ms for short prompts; 95th pct tail < 400ms.
3) Eval artifacts: we will run an automated pass over the prompt set attached (clearMed_prompt_set_v2.md) and produce CSV metrics (sample attached). We'll also include a small human-eval slice for edge cases you flagged.

Next steps I propose this week:
- You confirm permission to run the eval on the 2k transcript sample (we will redact PHI before processing).
- RedTeam: we run the baseline with rw-guanaco-13b-q4 and a smaller rw-instruct-3b fallback to measure costs and latency.
- We deliver a short report + demo video with streaming traces and a short list of 8 recommended prompt fixes.

Attachments: prompt set + quick benchmark template.

If that sounds good I can loop in our engineer for the canary run and schedule a 30-min sync next Tue.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0197

From: Anna Park <anna.park@clearmedhealth.com>

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the concise recap. A few quick things:

1) Clear to run the eval on the 2k sample; we'll need a short data processing agreement addendum — procurement copied (procurement@clearmedhealth.com).
2) Curious about human-eval: can you outline how many human judgments you recommend (we have limited SME time) and the turnaround?
3) For the stop-sequence checks, our forms use an explicit delimiter "<<<END_FORM>>>" — we'll expect a very high pass rate there.

If you can share a proposed pilot timeline and a minimal DocuSign for the data usage addendum, I'll get procurement to prioritize.

— Anna

Subject: RE: Post-call: capability summary + streaming coherence & eval plan — proposed eval runbook

Folks — drafting the eval runbook here so we can send a single artifact to Anna and procurement. Main points:

1) Data handling- We will run only on the 2k transcript CSV. Preprocessing steps: PII redaction (names -> [REDACTED], dates generalized to month/year), remove full SSNs, hash identifiers. Processing will be done in a private tenant and logs will be ephemeral.

2) Evaluation slices (automated):
- Stop-sequence pass-rate: run scripted prompts with your form delimiter ("<<<END_FORM>>>") and check if model emits that native token or a correct termination. Output: pass_rate per model.
- Partial-output coherence detection: heuristic that flags mid-output truncations where the last emitted token is mid-token or where the final sentence fragment is <8 chars but user-facing (we'll also run a simple language-model-based coherence scorer). Output: incoherent_event_rate per 1k responses.
- Latency profiling: measure time-to-first-token (TTFT) and per-token median across the prompt distribution (we'll collect 1k warm requests to populate percentiles).

3) Human eval (light-touch):
- 120 judgments (3 judgments per prompt on a 40-prompt stratified sample) focusing on: helpfulness, partial-output harm (did the partial output cause a misleading step), and stop-sequence correctness. We can recruit nurses/SMEs on your side or we can run via our panel; cost and turnaround: 3–5 business days if Redwood-run; 1–2 wks if cleared SMEs from ClearMed.

4) Models & configuration to run:
- Baseline: rw-guanaco-13b-q4 (streaming enabled, prefix caching on)
- Cheap fallback: rw-instruct-3b (no KV cache, minimal context)
- Upper bound: rw-llama-70b-q8 (streaming with quantized kernels)
- Routing policy: prefer 13b for standard traffic, route to 70b for flagged medical-answer prompts during canary.

5) Deliverables (5 business days from go):
- CSV: redwood_streaming_benchmarks_20270803.csv (auto metrics)
- Short report: 3 slides + 90s demo video of a streaming session showing a partial-output failure and proposed prompt mitigation.
- Prompt fixes: inline changes to 8 prompts (attached).

6) Risk notes:
- Stop-sequence mismatches are often caused by tokenization boundary differences between prompt templates and model vocab; we'll include normalized token checks.
- Streaming incoherence can be amplified by aggressive truncation settings; we'll test graceful end-of-sequence behavior and adjust the stop token heuristics.

I'll attach the CSV template and the sample prompt set (attached here). If you want I can convert the runbook into a one-page SOW to attach to the DocuSign.

-Jasmine
Product Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
